run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T03:55:42Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by a ~2.5 minute checkout outage caused by a Kubernetes rollout restart of the single-replica payment deployment. At 2026-11-15T03:55:59Z the payment deployment's pod template was annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:55:59Z, a new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 was created, and the only old pod (payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4) was deleted at 03:56:02Z. The payment container has no readinessProbe/startupProbe and the deployment allows maxUnavailable 25% (=1 of 1 replica), so the old pod was removed immediately while the new container had only just started and its gRPC server did not log 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' until 03:57:13.877Z; the first charge request reached it at 03:58:35.116Z. In exactly that interval the checkout path failed: checkout recorded ERROR spans only on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client call oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, frontend recorded ERROR spans only on POST /api/checkout, its internal route span and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and frontend-proxy recorded ERROR spans on ingress and router frontend egress. Checkout's logs from 03:56:05 to 03:57:18 show only '[PlaceOrder]' lines with no 'payment went through'/'order placed', and the normal success sequence resumes at 03:58:36. payment's own ERROR span series stayed 0 for the whole window and its logs show only successful Charge/Transaction pairs after start, so payment's application was not failing; the failure was the restart-induced unavailability of its single endpoint. 1-minute error buckets confine the burst to 03:56:30-03:58:30 with zero new errors afterwards, consistent with a transient, now-ended event; residual alert relevance is limited to small pre-existing ingress-only frontend-proxy error spans.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded ERROR-status spans on exactly two operations in the window: ingress (1h increase 12.40 at 03:55:42 rising to 76.27/78.22 later) and router frontend egress (0 at 03:55:42 rising to 60.0/59.94); the egress errors had no counterpart before the burst.

frontend's ERROR spans were confined to the checkout path: POST (59.98/h), POST /api/checkout (59.98/h), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (59.98/h) and client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (59.98/h); frontend's other operations (GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, CartService/GetCart, AdService/GetAds, tcp.connect) show 0 error increase across the window.

checkout's ERROR spans were confined to oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (23.22/h) and its client call oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (23.22/h); checkout's ERROR series is not returned for the 03:55:42 step and first appears at the 04:00:42 step with 54.67/h (absence is unknown, not zero).

1-minute error-span buckets localize the event to the 03:56:30-03:58:30 period: frontend 296 then 176 error spans, frontend-proxy 156 then 82, checkout 88 in the 03:57:30-03:58:30 bucket, with 0 in the buckets before and after (only isolated 2-span frontend-proxy buckets at 03:47, 03:49:30, 03:55:30 and 03:59:30).

The payment deployment was rolled out at 03:55:59-03:56:02: Deployment payment event 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' at 03:55:59, pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled 03:55:59 and container Started 03:56:02, and simultaneously 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0', ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete of pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 and 'Stopping container payment' at 03:56:02 (a controller-driven rollout, not an eviction or crash).

The payment deployment's pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:55:59Z; it runs 1 replica with strategy RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and the payment container has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (resources limits cpu 20m, memory 160Mi).

The rollout was configuration/annotation-only: old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 and new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and the same env set (PAYMENT_PORT 8080, OTEL_*, FLAGD_HOST/PORT).

The replacement payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 2026-11-15T03:57:13.877Z, about 71 seconds after its container start (03:56:02) and after the old pod had already been removed (03:56:02).

Between 03:56:05 and 03:57:18 the checkout container logged 45 lines, all of them '[PlaceOrder]', with no 'payment went through', 'order placed' or 'order confirmation email sent' lines, i.e. PlaceOrder started but never completed the payment step.

The new payment pod received its first 'Charge request received.' at 2026-11-15T03:58:35.116Z followed immediately by 'Transaction complete.'; checkout's normal success sequence ('[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent') resumes from 03:58:36.263Z onward.

payment itself recorded no ERROR spans: its ERROR series for charge, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, tls.connect and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge are 0 across the window, while its UNSET-status charge spans rose from 844.06 to 1211.01 per 1h window and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge from 843.83 to 1210.82.

payment was the only otel-demo pod that changed during the window: all other 20 pods started 03:22:59-03:24:48 with restartCount 0 (frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc 03:22:59, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 03:23:01, checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt 03:23:01), while payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht started 03:55:59 with restartCount 0 and is Running/ready.

A sampled successful checkout trace at 03:44:06 (before the burst) shows the observed call path load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy ingress -> frontend-proxy router frontend egress -> frontend POST -> POST /api/checkout -> grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge -> payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, all with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and http.status_code=200.

Other services show only small steady error counts that do not jump with the burst: ad ~2.05/h (1.05 -> 2.07 -> 2.04), fraud-detection ~2.04/h, recommendation 3.05 -> 4.06/h, accounting 0 and payment 0 across the window, versus frontend 0 -> 239.69/h, frontend-proxy 12.40 -> 138.16/h and checkout first returned at 54.67/h.

Primary cause: the payment rollout restart removed the only serving payment endpoint before the new container was actually serving, so checkout's Charge calls failed, checkout returned errors for PlaceOrder, frontend returned errors for /api/checkout, frontend-proxy logged ingress and router frontend egress errors, and the frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert fired. The 03:56:02 deletion, the 03:57:13.877 gRPC-server start log and the 03:56:30-03:58:30 error buckets coincide, and no other pod changed.

Contributing mechanism: because the payment container defines no readinessProbe/startupProbe and the deployment allows maxUnavailable 25% of 1 replica, the ReplicaSet counted the new pod as available as soon as its container started (03:56:02) and scaled the old pod to 0 at 03:56:02, while the application only began listening on 8080 at 03:57:13.877; adding a readiness/startup probe and disallowing unavailability would keep traffic on a serving pod.

Secondary candidate: frontend-proxy already had small ingress-only error counts before the restart (12.40 per 1h window at 03:55:42, isolated 2-span buckets at 03:47, 03:49:30 and 03:55:30, with router frontend egress errors still 0), so an alert threshold of 'error rate > 0' could in principle react to that pre-existing noise; this cannot be confirmed because the alert rule expression was not retrievable.

Unverified contributor: the payment container's cpu limit of 20m may have slowed application startup (71s from container start to 'payment gRPC server started'), lengthening the gap; no CPU throttling or startup-timing metric for payment was retrieved, so this remains unproven.

payment's own application was not erroring: its ERROR span series are 0 for every operation in the window, its logs after the restart contain only 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs, and its charge span volume increased rather than dropped (844 -> 1211 per 1h window).

Rejected: payment pod was OOM-killed, evicted or crash-looped. The old pod was removed by its own ReplicaSet ('SuccessfulDelete', reason Killing of a controller-managed rollout) at the same moment the new ReplicaSet was created at 03:55:59-03:56:02, and the new pod has restartCount 0; no Evicted or OOMKilled evidence appeared.

Rejected as the cause: another otel-demo dependency (cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, email, kafka, ad, fraud-detection, recommendation). The error spans are confined to the payment leg of the checkout path; in the sampled trace all other client calls carry rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and the only services with elevated error counts are frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout, whose errors all sit on the payment call.

Add a readinessProbe (e.g. grpc_health_probe against port 8080) and a startupProbe to the payment container and consider maxUnavailable: 0 plus more than one payment replica, so a restart of the single replica never removes the only serving endpoint before the new process listens.

Find out who/what issued the kubectl rollout restart on payment at 03:55:59Z (the restartedAt annotation) so an operator-induced restart of a single-replica dependency is scheduled or gated; change history is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: The alert rule expression, threshold and evaluation window could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules (rule_name filter and unfiltered both no_data), so the reported value 0.0111 and the exact firing instant cannot be reproduced.

The alert anchor 2026-11-15T03:55:42Z precedes the payment restartedAt annotation 2026-11-15T03:55:59Z by 17s; the measured error burst begins in the 03:56:30-03:57:30 bucket. The rule definition needed to explain this offset is missing.

Jaeger returned no spans after ~03:44:07 (source_end_at of the returned traces) and searches for frontend POST /api/checkout in 04:05-04:15 returned no traces, so the error-span tags of the failing calls (e.g. gRPC status code / error message such as UNAVAILABLE or connection refused) are not directly observed.

The deleted old payment pod's logs and previous-container instance are unavailable (pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 no longer exists; previous container not found), so what it logged or whether it in-flight-failed during termination is unknown.

The exact change that produced the new payment pod template hash is unknown: image and env are identical between payment-55766d76b9 and payment-7b6bfb9fb4, and only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation and an unrelated openshift.io/required-scc annotation are visible on the template.
No change_history integration is available, so the actor and reason for the payment rollout restart cannot be established.

Prometheus series for the footprint only start around 03:55:42 (source_start_at) with data_as_of up to ~04:07 in several views, so no longer baseline before the window exists to compare the magnitude of the error burst against earlier periods.

No ERROR series was returned for cart, currency, email, product-catalog, shipping, quote or kafka, so their error state during the burst is unknown rather than zero; they were not individually verified beyond the single sampled pre-burst trace.
The frontend container returned no log lines for the burst window, so frontend-side error text is unverified.
No CPU throttling or container startup-duration metric for the payment container was retrieved, so the effect of its 20m CPU limit on the 71s startup delay is unverified.
next_steps: Review why a kubectl rollout restart was applied to the payment deployment at 2026-11-15T03:55:59Z (deployment change history / GitOps or operator audit log outside this Run).

Add a gRPC readiness/startup probe to the payment container and set maxUnavailable: 0 (or run more than one payment replica) to prevent a restart of the single replica from removing the only serving endpoint.
Check the alert rule definition for RequestErrorRate (its query, threshold and window) in Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files, since the rule set was not readable here.

If the small pre-existing ingress-only frontend-proxy error spans (~12/h, egress 0) are considered noise, confirm whether the rule should exclude ingress-only status classes to avoid warning alerts from baseline errors.
